{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABYczS4w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhCA2fk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 17, "title": "Expand Weave BASIC compatibility with classic MSX BASIC programming features", "body": "## Problem

Weave BASIC is an independently written Rust interpreter backed by the emulated MSX1 VDP/PSG and its original Z80 boot firmware. Its current `PRINT`, `IF`, `GOTO`, `FOR/NEXT`, `SCREEN`, `PSET` and `SOUND` support makes it useful for demonstrations, but it cannot run many ordinary childhood-era MSX BASIC listings: key control-flow, input, array, data and graphics statements are missing.

We want the publicly available, ROM-free browser experience to feel increasingly like **classic Microsoft/ASCII MSX BASIC**, without bundling, deriving or copying proprietary MSX BASIC ROMs, binaries, disassemblies, source code, token tables or other copyrighted implementation assets. The desired outcome is meaningful source-level compatibility and a familiar programming experience, **not** a claim to be the original product or a byte-for-byte/binary-compatible BIOS.

## Expected outcome

Extend the existing **Weave BASIC** to run a well-defined, useful set of original classic-style MSX BASIC programs involving subroutines, arrays, keyboard input, data statements and common screen graphics, with behavior close to documented MSX BASIC 1.x syntax and observable semantics on the currently supported MSX1 screen modes.

Maintain Weave BASIC as original, MIT-licensed Rust code, using independently authored tests and public language/hardware specifications. Retain the existing Weave BASIC branding, while making supported syntax feel familiar to people who learned BASIC on an MSX. A complete MSX BASIC 1.0/2.0 implementation, original ROM execution, proprietary ROM redistribution and binary/tokenized program compatibility are **not** prerequisites of this Issue.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`, `main`; see `crates/msx-core/src/basic.rs`, `crates/msx-core/tests/basic.rs`, `crates/msx-core/src/firmware.rs`, `web/app.js`, `tests/browser.spec.js` and README's **Weave BASIC and firmware** section.
- Currently documented limitations include no arrays, `INPUT`, `GOSUB`, `ELSE`, `DATA`, disk/tape/file operations or MSX BIOS API. Graphics offers `PSET` on `SCREEN 2/3` but not `LINE`, `CIRCLE` or `PAINT`.
- The user wants to recreate the experience of writing BASIC programs on a childhood MSX, while keeping a legal, ROM-free, publicly playable browser demo.
- MSX2 currently uses bundled BSD-licensed C-BIOS to boot cartridges, **not** Microsoft MSX BASIC; preserve it and the user's ability to load their own lawful external BIOS/BASIC ROMs. Weave BASIC remains the original MSX1 built-in interpreter.
- The source language's documented commands, syntax and observable behavior are compatible targets; third-party implementations and ROM contents must **not** be copied. Record the public specifications used and any deliberate deviations.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Core language and program semantics

- [ ] Add `GOSUB` / `RETURN` including nested subroutines, end-of-program/error behavior, direct/numbered statements where applicable, and interaction with existing `GOTO`, `IF ... THEN`, `FOR/NEXT`, `RUN`, `NEW`, `STOP` and Escape/BREAK. Preserve the cooperative frame-yield behavior for long or infinite programs.
- [ ] Implement `DIM` and indexed numeric/string arrays with explicit size limits, indexing/range validation and clear type-mismatch/subscript errors. Document supported dimensions and reset semantics. Preserve existing scalar variable behavior.
- [ ] Add `DATA`, `READ` and `RESTORE` with deterministic traversal in program-line order, string/numeric assignments, exhaustion/type errors, and reset/restore behavior. Make inline data syntax and statement separation work with numbered program lines.
- [ ] Add interactive `INPUT` (optional prompt and one or more variables as reasonably supported) using the existing emulated keyboard and text input path. While waiting for input, do not block the browser, spin endlessly, lose keyboard focus or prevent Escape/BREAK and Reset. Handle invalid numeric input and cancellation in a predictable, documented way.
- [ ] Align the supported subset's syntax and observable behavior with published MSX BASIC conventions wherever feasible: line numbers and colon-separated statements, expressions, variable types, `PRINT` punctuation, errors and program state. Fix directly relevant compatibility gaps found by the independent sample programs without rewriting the interpreter unnecessarily.

### Graphics and authentic user experience

- [ ] Support classic `LINE` and `CIRCLE` graphics statements in suitable existing modes, plus bounded `PAINT` flood-fill, with clearly specified MSX BASIC-style argument forms and color behavior. Perform drawing through the **emulated VDP/VRAM**, not by painting an unrelated HTML Canvas overlay. Preserve `PSET`, `SCREEN`, `COLOR` and existing graphics limits.
- [ ] Include at least **three original, freely redistributable, runnable BASIC examples** exercising (1) `GOSUB` plus array/data processing, (2) interactive `INPUT`, and (3) `LINE`/`CIRCLE`/`PAINT` graphics. Make them readily discoverable in the browser or documentation without cluttering the display-first UI. Users should be able to copy/type the examples into the built-in BASIC environment and run them.
- [ ] Keep the MSX1 Weave BASIC editor and prompt, listing/editing programs, keyboard behavior, on-screen display and PSG output working. Explain clearly that this is **Weave BASIC, an independently implemented MSX BASIC-inspired interpreter**, not Microsoft's original MSX BASIC.
- [ ] Update `HELP`, the README and browser help with accurate examples, supported syntax, known deviations and compatibility limits. Remove now-outdated claims about missing features actually implemented in this Issue.

### Rights, scope and automated verification

- [ ] Write the interpreter additions, graphical primitives, fixtures and examples independently under this repository's MIT license. Do not download, embed, translate, reconstruct or reverse-engineer proprietary Microsoft/ASCII MSX BASIC code/ROMs; do not copy GPL implementation code or assume publicly visible ROMs are freely redistributable. Ordinary syntax/behavior may be described and independently implemented from lawful public documentation.
- [ ] Add Rust unit/integration tests with exact expected output/state and error results for each language feature; cover nested control flow, repeated `RUN`, variable and data resets, array bounds, input acceptance/retry/interrupt, invalid syntax, infinite-program yielding and non-regression of existing statements. Graphics tests must inspect actual emulated VRAM/pixels, including clipping/fill termination.
- [ ] Add Playwright browser/Wasm tests that type and execute original programs through the actual emulator input UI, assert visible screen output and graphics pixels, exercise an interactive `INPUT` sequence, and verify Reset/BREAK behavior. Run existing MSX1/MSX2 C-BIOS, cartridge, mapper and GitHub Pages-path regressions.
- [ ] Execute and report the repository's applicable automated checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs` and `npm test`. No original proprietary ROM, human hardware, subjective comparison or owner gameplay is required for PR review/merge.
- [ ] Keep the change focused on the above **complete usable subset**. Do **not** require full MSX BASIC 2.0 syntax, `PLAY`/music macro language, sprite language, disk/tape/file I/O, tokenized binary `.BAS` support, an exact numeric representation, MSX2 BASIC in C-BIOS mode, or undocumented BIOS hooks; such work can receive a separate Issue when needed.

## Optional validation

After merge, the owner can type in remembered MSX BASIC programs or legally available example listings to evaluate the nostalgic programming experience. Record unsupported syntax or behavioral mismatches as separate follow-up Issues; subjective human testing is **not** a merge gate. Additional public-language reference comparisons are welcome if their code is not copied.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] Confirm the deployed GitHub Pages build at https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ includes the merged Weave BASIC changes, boots in MSX1 and runs the original subroutine/data and graphics examples with visible output. Record the actual deployment run, URL and observed result. This live check follows merge and cannot block PR approval; defects found afterward become new Issues.
